hypothesis: MTP speculation becomes a net speedup once the heads are trained on verifier-proven frames.

verdict.note: Speculation is lossless but is not a speedup on this core. Both quantitative gates fail; the speed claim rests on the non-speculative engine and Engine.generate/generate_batch now default to speculative=False.

negative_results: First two corpus builds wrote nothing: block-buffered stdout with end-only persistence. Fixed with per-task flush and incremental records/frames.

Ten verifier timeouts (final_failed=999) caused by third-party pytest plugin autoload shadowing workspace module names; archived verbatim in records-failed-timeouts.jsonl, root-caused and retried successfully.
Speculation skipped prompt bytes and left accepted drafts unwritten in gen_out; both fixed and pinned by tests/test_core.py::test_native_v2_speculation_is_lossless.

Speculation lost byte identity whenever a draft occupied the final token of a patch (coarse hand-off): traced to a copy-gate state divergence at the following patch boundary. Drafts are now confined to non-final patch positions; the full-K variant is recorded as a defect, not silently dropped.

Engine acceptance rate (accepted/attempted, 38.0%/35.8%) differs from the pre-registered mean_prefix/K metric (29.3%/27.5%); both reported. Engine metric is higher because drafts 2..K are only attempted after draft 1 matches.
Speculation is 0.87x-0.92x the non-speculative speed: draft projections and batched copy steps cost more than the fine-path batching saves at ~38% acceptance.

cost.lost_build_attempts: two runs timed out at 1800 s each with no output before resumability was added
